In the early 1990s, the Portuguese neuroscientist was among the first to publish research suggesting that feelings such as hunger and pain might provide the foundations for consciousness, that familiar experience of being alive, awake, and self-aware in the world.Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 10 NASA And The Government Shutdown On 'This Week In Space'ShareNextStayToday, Damasio has plenty of scientific company in his empirical approach to consciousness. But among consciousness researchers there are many prominent and conflicting theories of what consciousness is and how it functions, which differ significantly. Damasio belongs to the camp that believes that consciousness requires a body. Other theorists argue that all you need is sophisticated information processing architecture, which could exist without any kind of fleshy home. Read More: “What’s So Hard About Understanding Consciousness?”Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
